BBC: Zack Polanski faces greatest crisis of his leadership so far. By Chris Mason, political editor. JSON-LD datePublished 2026-10-09T04:54:25Z (05:54 BST); dateModified 06:35:56Z (07:35 BST).
'In the aftermath of a by-election, the focus is usually on the winner. Not this time.'
On Abdi-Wali: arrived in the UK as a child refugee from Somalia in the 1990s, grew up locally in Camden, became a councillor four years ago, council leader in May, now Starmer's successor as MP.
'This constituency has long been a safe Labour seat - the political home of the former prime minister and before that the former cabinet minister Frank Dobson. So a Labour victory here falls in the column marked "relief" for Downing Street rather than "jubilation".'
'His failure to win here will prompt questions from some about stalling momentum, but the party can and does point to the big swing to them since the general election and a result that was by a long way the second best ever result for them at a Westminster by-election.'
PARTY-SYSTEM DETAIL: 'Incidentally, in finishing third the Conservatives have beaten Reform UK for the first time in an English by-election since the general election. It seems likely that Reform's result was hampered by Restore Britain, who managed almost half as many votes as Reform did, in a constituency not very favourable to either party.'
Mason was at Camden Council offices at 3am; the press pack's focus was on Polanski, not the winner.
'But the real reason for the nocturnal scramble of cameras, microphones and questions for Polanski had little to do with the by-election - and everything to do with a vote at the Green Party's conference in Brighton last weekend.'
Polanski 'repeatedly declined to do interviews, as the pressure on him ratcheted up. But this morning he did speak to journalists.'
